title: dir — List Directory Contents
description: The dir command lists files and folders in a directory, with sizes and timestamps. Switches control paging, wide format, sorting, and recursion into subdirectories. It is the first command every cmd user learns.
batch_snippet:
@echo off
dir C:\Windows /o:-s /p
echo ---
dir *.log /s /b | find /c ".log"

demo.program:
@echo off
dir C:\Windows /o:-s /p
echo ---
dir *.log /s /b | find /c ".log"

provenance: Public record compiled from manufacturer-published specifications and public product documentation; cross-checked against multiple public sources.

title: cd — Change Directory
description: The cd command moves between directories; cd.. goes up one level and cd\ jumps to the drive root. The /d switch changes drive and directory in one step. Typing cd alone prints the current directory.
batch_snippet:
@echo off
cd /d C:\Windows\System32
echo Current: %CD%
cd..
echo Up one: %CD%

demo.program:
@echo off

provenance: Public record compiled from manufacturer-published specifications and public product documentation; cross-checked against multiple public sources.

title: cls — Clear Screen
description: The cls command wipes the console screen, leaving a clean prompt at the top. It does not clear command history — press F7 to see that. Useful before demos and screenshots.
batch_snippet:
@echo off
echo Screen will clear in 2 seconds...
timeout /t 2 >nul
cls
echo Fresh screen.

title: copy — Copy Files
description: The copy command duplicates files, and can concatenate several sources into one destination with the + operator. /y suppresses overwrite prompts; /-y forces them. It handles single files simply; xcopy or robocopy suit trees.
provenance: Public record compiled from manufacturer-published specifications and public product documentation; cross-checked against multiple public sources.

title: xcopy — Extended Copy
description: The xcopy command copies whole directory trees, unlike plain copy. /s copies subdirectories, /e includes empty ones, /h grabs hidden files, and /d copies only files changed since a date. It remains handy for quick mirrors.
provenance: Public record compiled from manufacturer-published specifications and public product documentation; cross-checked against multiple public sources.

title: robocopy — Robust Copy
description: Robocopy is Windows' industrial file copier: multi-threaded, restartable, and able to mirror entire trees with /mir. /z resumes interrupted copies and /r:/w control retry behavior. Always test /mir on a copy first — it deletes destination files not in the source.
provenance: Public record compiled from manufacturer-published specifications and public product documentation; cross-checked against multiple public sources.

title: del — Delete Files
description: The del command deletes files — permanently, bypassing the Recycle Bin. /f forces read-only files, /s walks subdirectories, and /q skips confirmation. There is no undo, so echo the file list with dir first when unsure.
provenance: Public record compiled from manufacturer-published specifications and public product documentation; cross-checked against multiple public sources.

title: mkdir and rmdir — Make/Remove Directories
description: mkdir creates directories, including nested paths in one call. rmdir removes empty directories; /s deletes a directory tree with everything inside it. The short forms md and rd work identically.
batch_snippet:
@echo off
mkdir C:\Demo\a\b\c
echo Tree created.
rmdir /s /q C:\Demo
echo Tree removed.

provenance: Public record compiled from manufacturer-published specifications and public product documentation; cross-checked against multiple public sources.

title: move — Move Files
description: The move command relocates files or renames directories, working across drives by copying then deleting. /y suppresses overwrite prompts. Moving within one drive is instant since only the directory entry changes.
provenance: Public record compiled from manufacturer-published specifications and public product documentation; cross-checked against multiple public sources.

title: ren — Rename Files
description: The ren command renames files and directories; wildcards let you rename batches, like ren *.txt *.md. The destination is a name only, not a path — use move to relocate. It is instant and safe.
provenance: Public record compiled from manufacturer-published specifications and public product documentation; cross-checked against multiple public sources.

title: type — Display File Contents
description: The type command prints a text file to the console. Pipe it into more for paging or findstr for searching. It only handles text sensibly — binary files produce garbage.
provenance: Public record compiled from manufacturer-published specifications and public product documentation; cross-checked against multiple public sources.

title: echo — Display Messages
description: The echo command prints text, and @echo off at the top of a batch file silences command echoing for clean output. Redirect with > to write files and >> to append. echo. prints a blank line.
batch_snippet:
@echo off
echo Starting backup...
echo.
echo Done.

title: find and findstr — Search Text
description: findstr searches files for text with far more power than find: /s recurses, /i ignores case, /n shows line numbers, and /r enables regex. It is the cmd equivalent of grep for quick log hunting.
provenance: Public record compiled from manufacturer-published specifications and public product documentation; cross-checked against multiple public sources.

title: ipconfig — IP Configuration
description: The ipconfig command shows network adapter addresses, masks, and gateways; /all adds DNS, DHCP, and MAC details. /release and /renew cycle a DHCP lease, and /flushdns clears the resolver cache — the classic first step for network trouble.
batch_snippet:
@echo off
ipconfig /flushdns
ipconfig /renew
echo Network refreshed.

title: ping — Test Connectivity
description: The ping command sends ICMP echo requests to test reachability and measure round-trip time. -n sets the count, -t pings until stopped, and -l changes packet size. 'Request timed out' versus 'Destination unreachable' point at different problems.
provenance: Public record compiled from manufacturer-published specifications and public product documentation; cross-checked against multiple public sources.

title: tracert — Trace Route
description: The tracert command maps every hop between you and a target, showing where latency or loss appears. -d skips slow reverse-DNS lookups and -h caps the hop count. Sudden timeouts mid-trace usually mean a router that ignores ICMP, not a failure.
provenance: Public record compiled from manufacturer-published specifications and public product documentation; cross-checked against multiple public sources.

title: netstat — Network Statistics
description: The netstat command lists active connections and listening ports; -a shows all, -n uses numeric addresses, -o adds the owning process ID, and -b names the executable. Pair -o with tasklist to identify mystery listeners.
provenance: Public record compiled from manufacturer-published specifications and public product documentation; cross-checked against multiple public sources.

title: tasklist and taskkill — Process Control
syntax: tasklist [/fi filter] [/fo format]  |  taskkill [/f] [/pid n | /im name]
description: tasklist shows running processes with PIDs and memory use; taskkill ends them by PID or image name, with /f forcing the kill. /fi filters like "memusage gt 500000" find resource hogs. Always try without /f first.
batch_snippet:
@echo off
tasklist /fi "imagename eq notepad.exe" | findstr notepad >nul
if %errorlevel%==0 taskkill /im notepad.exe /f
echo Done.

title: sfc — System File Checker
description: The sfc command scans protected Windows system files and repairs corruption from a cached copy. /scannow both scans and repairs and needs an elevated prompt. Run DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth first if sfc cannot fix files.
batch_snippet:
@echo off
:: Run as Administrator
sfc /scannow
echo Exit code: %ERRORLEVEL%

title: chkdsk — Check Disk
description: The chkdsk command checks filesystem integrity; /f fixes errors, /r locates bad sectors and recovers data, and /x forces a dismount. /r on large drives can take hours — schedule it overnight. Run it when disks act strangely or after crashes.
batch_snippet:
@echo off
:: Run as Administrator
chkdsk C: /scan
echo Scan complete.

title: diskpart — Disk Partitioning
description: diskpart is Windows' command-line partition manager: list disk, select disk, then clean, convert, create partition, format, and assign. Script mode with /s automates wipes. It obeys instantly with no undo — selecting the wrong disk is catastrophic, so list twice.
batch_snippet:
select disk 1
clean
convert gpt
create partition primary
format fs=ntfs quick label=Data
assign letter=E

title: shutdown — Shutdown and Restart
description: The shutdown command powers off (/s), restarts (/r), logs off (/l), or hibernates (/h) with an optional /t delay; /a aborts a pending shutdown. /m targets a remote machine. /f forces apps closed — save work first.
provenance: Public record compiled from manufacturer-published specifications and public product documentation; cross-checked against multiple public sources.

title: systeminfo — System Information
description: The systeminfo command dumps a full hardware and OS report: version, install date, uptime, RAM, and hotfixes. Pipe it to findstr to pull single facts like OS Name or System Boot Time. /s queries remote machines.
provenance: Public record compiled from manufacturer-published specifications and public product documentation; cross-checked against multiple public sources.

title: set and path — Environment Variables
description: The set command displays or changes environment variables for the current session; setx makes them permanent. path controls where cmd searches for programs. Changes in one window never affect others — use setx or the GUI for permanence.
batch_snippet:
@echo off
set MYAPP_HOME=C:\MyApp
set PATH=%MYAPP_HOME%\bin;%PATH%
echo %MYAPP_HOME%

title: for — Loop Command
syntax: for %v in (set) do command  |  for /f ["opts"] %v in (file/'cmd') do command  |  for /l %v in (start,step,end)
description: The for command loops over files, numbers, or command output — the heart of batch scripting. In batch files use %%v instead of %v. /f parses file lines or command output with tokens and delimiters; /l counts numerically; /r walks directory trees.
provenance: Public record compiled from manufacturer-published specifications and public product documentation; cross-checked against multiple public sources.
